description: The Canadian Active Control System (CACS) is the national network of continuously tracking GNSS stations of the Canadian Geodetic Survey, called active control points, each with a high-precision dual-frequency receiver and a geodetic antenna, some with an atomic frequency standard. The web application lets users download station coordinates, metadata and GNSS observation data for the national network and for regional, provincial and municipal networks whose data the Survey distributes. Users select stations on a map or list and download RINEX 2 or RINEX 3/4 observations at 30-second or 1-second intervals for chosen dates and hours, for all GNSS or GPS or GLONASS only, with optional precise orbits (NAD83 (CSRS) or ITRF), broadcast ephemerides and clock corrections, as zip or tar archives; station lists come as KML, CSV or PDF reports, with positioning time series per station. Access is free online, with an account sign-in; the Government of Canada terms apply and no separate licence is named on the page read. Caveats: the map was temporarily unavailable when read, though station selection still worked. Coverage is Canada. It supports positioning infrastructure studies, crustal deformation monitoring and space weather effects on GNSS; the related record is PositioNZ of New Zealand, and it complements the CSRS-PPP service catalogued by another piece.
